The client generates a cryptographic code verifier and derives a code challenge, sending the challenge with the initial authorization request and the verifier during token exchange to prove client authenticity. OpenID Connect (OIDC) extends this flow by issuing a cryptographically signed ID Token (JWT) that provides verifiable identity claims alongside the OAuth access token. In modern SPAs, storing access and refresh tokens in localStorage is avoided due to XSS vulnerabilities; instead, tokens should be handled via secure backend-for-frontend (BFF) proxies or stored in HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure cookies with rotating refresh tokens.
